walkthroughs.body_html:
The People's Health c1250 to Present — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The People's Health c1250 to Present brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The People's Health c1250 to Present.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which event triggered Bazalgette's sewer system?
options: Cholera epidemic 1854
Great Stink 1858
Great Fire 1666
Typhoid outbreak 1860

mcqs.q: What did Magna Carta actually do in 1215?
options: It was a peace treaty between King John and rebel barons protecting baronial privileges and limiting arbitrary royal taxation and imprisonment — it was annulled within months.
Magna Carta gave ordinary English people democratic rights and freedom.
Magna Carta abolished the monarchy and created Parliament.
Cities were unhealthy because factory smoke poisoned the food.

mcqs.q: What were the Wars of the Roses really about?
options: The whole country was at war for thirty continuous years.
Dynastic conflict between rival branches of the Plantagenets (Lancaster and York) over the throne, intensified by weak kingship under Henry VI and noble factionalism.
They were a religious war between Catholics and Protestants.
Cities were unhealthy because factory smoke poisoned the food.

mcqs.q: Why were 19th-century industrial cities so unhealthy?
options: Rapid population growth outpaced housing, water and sewage; lack of regulation produced overcrowded slums and cholera epidemics until reforms followed Chadwick's 1842 report.
Magna Carta abolished the monarchy and created Parliament.
Cities were unhealthy because factory smoke poisoned the food.
Cities were unhealthy because Victorians did not care about hygiene.
